verdict.rationale: Bento documents event-triggered rules for its observability domain: alerts written in plain English compile to trace queries, fire in real time on matching events, and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook. Rules also live in the repo as YAML, and the product mentions trigger-based fixes. The automated actions documented are mostly notification and routing, and trigger-based fixes are named but not explained, so the story is only partly covered. Missing for 10: documented actions beyond alert routing (general automated remediation workflows), detail on the rule/trigger syntax and how webhook delivery is configured, and independent or hands-on corroboration that rules fire and act as claimed.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Alerts are defined in plain natural language... Rules compile to trace queries and route to Slack, PagerDuty, email, or webhook.
